prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B060 with Buchwald and Hartwig. Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling is a mature, general, ligand-controlled method whose mechanism (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination) has been worked out with isolated intermediates and structural evidence, and which three decades of independent use in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis have confirmed. It is distinct from the 2010 prize, which honoured C-C coupling, and the citation can say carbon-nitrogen coupling explicitly to make that distinction part of the text. The attribution is two names, with Kosugi treated as a precursor whose tin-amide reaction was not a general catalytic method. This is the only preferred configuration on the table whose maturity, chemical identity and credit allocation I can all check against the record without a caveat.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that C-N coupling extends the palladium paradigm already honoured in 2010 and will look conservative next to a new modality. Five colleagues now prefer B026 with a single identical trio, and that is a serious signal about how the committee reads novelty. A Buchwald and Hartwig prize also rests on a priority history that is not perfectly tidy (Kosugi and Migita, and the near-simultaneous independent catalyst development), so the committee would have to accept the two-person cut as a judgment and not as a certainty.

responses.point: Brzezinski asked for my specific objection to B026, which I ranked eighth in the opening, and moved it up to his preferred configuration on the basis of measurable ternary-complex physics and a compact three-name attribution.
responses.response: My objection was maturity and attribution, not originality. I accept the physical argument: ternary-complex cooperativity, kinetics and structure are measured quantitatively, and approved cereblon-dependent glues show the principle works in patients, so I no longer treat the missing PROTAC approval as disqualifying. What remains for me is that the trio is a choice between decisive contributions. The structural work on how a ligase, a degrader and a target actually assemble is what made the heterobifunctional arm rationally designable, and I do not see the reports having shown that it can be left out. I will not oppose B026 on maturity, but I will not call it settled either.

responses.point: Aqvist argues that approval is the wrong test for a chemistry prize, and says he would hear a case for Ciulli replacing Deshaies, which echoes my own opening trio.
responses.response: On the standard I agree with you: independent replication, structural evidence and approved glues are enough to establish a principle. My case for Ciulli is a structural-evidence case. His VHL ligands and crystal structures of ligase-degrader-target complexes turned a concept into a design method, and in my field I would credit the group that showed how the assembly is built. But you and Linke are right that discovery precedes optimisation, so Crews, Deshaies and Handa are the more defensible core if the committee goes this way. If B026 is the final configuration I would ask that the report on Deshaies versus Ciulli be explicit, because that omission will draw the most criticism.

responses.point: Linke now treats B067 as a fall-back and keeps B026 as lead, while resisting a split of PROTACs and glues and conceding that excluding Ciulli will be criticised.
responses.response: I agree that one induced-proximity citation covers both arms, and that a split would only force a harder three-person cut. I do not think B067 is a better fall-back than B060 on the criteria you apply. Its reversible-terminator chemistry is separable on paper from 454 and Mayer, but the platform history is not, and it sits at the border with Physiology or Medicine. B060 has none of those allocation problems. If the committee wants a mature chemistry fall-back with two clean names, it is this one.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B060 with Buchwald and Hartwig, excludes Kosugi, and lists B026 as an alternative while warning that B060 may read as a continuation of 2010.
responses.response: We now match on laureates and on wording. I would answer the continuation objection in the citation and in the report: the 2010 prize rewarded forming C-C bonds, whereas C-N coupling needed its own ligand classes and mechanistic solutions, since amine binding and C-N reductive elimination behave very differently. I share your honesty that B060 has two supporters and B026 has five. Where I differ slightly is that I am less willing than you to concede that this is a question of novelty alone; the committee should also weigh that B060 needs no caveat on maturity or credit.

responses.point: Chabes argues that cereblon is not pharmacology only and that the ternary-complex mechanism is quantified in vitro, so degradation rests on tested chemistry.
responses.response: That is a fair reading and it is the main reason I have moved from opposing B026 to treating it as a defensible majority configuration. I would add that a chemical-terms citation should name induced proximity and ubiquitin-ligase recruitment and not any drug, so it stays on the chemistry. My remaining difference from you is weighting. I value a method whose scope and mechanism are fully in the open literature, and I count the unfinished PROTAC clinical record as a small but real cost.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see C-N coupling as a distinct achievement from the 2010 prize or as its continuation.
Whether a two-person B060 prize can win against a five-member B026 preference; I recognise that it probably cannot without a new argument.
Whether Ciulli, Deshaies or Sakamoto should be in the B026 trio; I have not seen the expert reports resolve this.
Whether the Buchwald and Hartwig priority history relative to Kosugi and Migita will be accepted as settled.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with B060 or its credited names is apparent from my profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which is not relevant to the candidates preferred here. I have a broad network in porous materials and electron crystallography that includes some credited people in B046, which I list only as an alternative, and I would recuse from any vote that depends on that candidacy. I disclose no tie to any credited name in B026 or B060.
